title.narrative: Support for agricultural micro-enterprises and integration in value chains to increase food security in Pakistan

description.narrative: Direct participants: 4500 households (31,500 residents / 16,906 men and 15,404 women) in selected rural areas of District Tharparkar and Thatta in Sind, i.e., 2000 in rice, 500 in fisheries and 2000 households in livestock value chain. It is envisaged that 30% of the target groups, which are also represented in the proposed three-tier group structure, will be women and 900 youth (both men and women) will be engaged.Indirect participants: 87044 residents of both districts.Institutes:(1) 3-tier community structures, of Farmers Enterprise Groups (FEGs), Farmers Market Collectives (FMCs) and Value Chain Associations (VCAs).(2) 2 Local partners,SAFWCO and SUKAAR Foundation.(3) Civil Society, trade associations and at least 7 government institutes and academia/research institutes.

Improving food and nutrition security of smallholder farmers and youth, MSME, value chain agribusiness in Pakistan targets the districts of Tharparkar and Thatta in Sind, Pakistan. According to the Food Insecurity Experience Scale (FIES), 64% of households in Thatta and 51% in Tharparkar face food insecurity. These districts are among the poorest in the country. Tharparkar has a significant livestock population, while Thatta ranks as the fifth largest rice producer in the region. Its coastal location and proximity to cities create opportunities for inland fisheries. The project aims to harness the economic potential of three value chains, fostering collective action and representation among farming communities. It focuses on improving both production and market -systems for rural farmers.

Overall Objective: Food security has improved in the districts of Thatta and Tharparkar in Sindh, Pakistan.Project Outcome:4,500 smallholder households in the districts of Thatta and Tharparkar realise their economic potential and stabilise their food situation.
